title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer (Zenodo record)
note: Software record v1.0.0 by D. Goehner (independent researcher), DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24010850, MIT licence, one 3.9 MB archive, supplement to the GitHub release. Four PJM cold events (Jan 2014, Feb 2015 as error anchor only, Dec 2017-Jan 2018, Dec 2022); three forecaster families x five conformal calibrators; day-ahead primary horizon, 1-hour reference. No other versions listed.

title: PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer (Zenodo record)
note: Headline findings on the record: uncalibrated 90% interval coverage collapses inside the events; no calibrator chosen without the target event restores nominal coverage (0 of 18 cells pass the repair judgement); retrospective leave-one-event-out evaluation overstates event coverage of the two Mondrian calibrators by 11.6 and 21.2 points. Says the protocol was frozen before results.

title: DresdenGman/PJM-Cold-Calibration-Benchmark (README)
note: MIT repo, one commit. Forecasters: quantile gradient boosting, linear-tree LightGBM, statistical location-scale model; no foundation models. Load: PJM metered load and EIA-930 PJM balancing-authority demand (RTO-wide, no zones). Weather: ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo, footprint mean. Python 3.11, seed 42; the 2014 modelling table is not redistributed and must be rebuilt.

title: DresdenGman/PJM-Cold-Calibration-Benchmark (README)
note: README numbers: day-ahead QR-GBT 90% coverage 12.5% in the 2014 vortex window vs 65.7% over 2014 (gap 53.2 points); gaps 14.3 (2017-18) and 9.2 (Elliott); best single repair is adaptive conformal on 2014 at 0.583 vs nominal 0.90; Mondrian overstatement 11.6 and 21.2 points. Notes the strictest J1 form narrowly missed on Elliott.

title: FREEZE_PROTOCOL.md (pre-registration, v2 with Amendment A1)
note: States v2 was frozen on 2026-11-05 at 21:02 US Pacific and Amendment A1 minutes later, before Run-1 results. The only proof is the document's own timestamp: no hash, registry or timestamping service. A1 splits C2 into C2a/C2b, fixes the fit/tune/calibration split and makes calibrator selection leave-one-event-out.

title: FREEZE_PROTOCOL.md (pre-registration, v2 with Amendment A1)
note: Day-ahead horizon: for each hour of day d only data before 10:00 EPT on d-1 (about 15 to 38 h lead); load lags are truncated by release time but weather is observed ERA5, a weather-oracle setup. The 1-hour horizon is an upper-bound reference. L1 sklearn HistGradientBoosting quantile model, 14 features; L2 LightGBM linear_tree, same features; L3 spline in temperature, HDH and 72 h thermal memory.

title: RESULTS_RUN1.md (Run 1 report, frozen protocol v2)
note: J1 does not hold as written: L1 day-ahead gaps are 53.2, 14.3 and 9.2 points, so the 10-point bar fails for 2022; replication by L2/L3 passes. J2 fails in all six horizon-by-learner cells under both selection schemes. J3 mean gaps for L1 day-ahead: C2a +11.6, C2b +21.2, others within about 1.3 points; smaller for L2 (5.1, 13.3), mixed for L3. Run date not stated.

title: RESULTS_RUN1.md (Run 1 report, frozen protocol v2)
note: Event windows: 2014 Jan 6-8 (72 h), 2017-18 Dec 28-Jan 7 (264 h), 2022 Dec 23-26 (96 h). Test spans: 2014 full year (8,760 h); 2018 and 2022 eras 2,156 h each. Uncalibrated L1 day-ahead event coverage 0.125, 0.439, 0.458, with wide block-bootstrap ranges (0.000-0.333 for 2014) that the report calls descriptive, not confidence intervals.

title: RESULTS_RUN1.md (Run 1 report, frozen protocol v2)
note: Stated deviations: event windows come from an earlier audit; a Jan-Nov 2022 load gap delays 2022 evaluation to Dec 8; some calibrators give infinite intervals (C2a's 1.000 coverage in 2022 rests on them); the 5-point replication bar, frontier interpolation and expansion factor are the author's own choices; L2 was shrunk to 120 rounds and 15 leaves for runtime on a 4-core VM.

title: DATA_SOURCES.md
note: Target is PJM-wide hourly load: PJM metered load 2010-2014 for the 2014 era, EIA-930 PJM balancing-authority demand for 2018 and 2022. Weather is ERA5 actuals (temperature, dew point, wind), equal-weight mean of 15 grid points; both horizons use realised weather. PJM official day-ahead peak errors: -1.81% (2014), -1.33% (2015), -3.90% (2017-18), -6.59% or -8,878 MW (Elliott).
